title: Soursop Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Soursop Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Soursop nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen and potassium in guyabano, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Soursop nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your guyabano (soursop) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, calcium, boron and magnesium. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Nitrogen deficiency on a leaf, shown on another crop as a stand in for soursop
heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But calcium and boron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which soursop nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Soursop nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a soursop nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest soursop nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in soursop

Older leaves near the base slowly lose their green and turn an even pale green over the blade, stalk and veins. As it gets worse all leaves turn yellow and lose their shine, the old leaves drop early. The plant stays short with a thin stem. In a Brazilian nutrient trial on guyabano, leaving out nitrogen hurt growth the most of all nutrients, cutting plant dry weight by 94 percent. You see it most at this stage: seedlings and young trees in fast growth, and bearing trees during fruit growth.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in guyabano
Sandy or eroded soils low in organic matter, trees that get no manure or fertilizer, and heavy rain that washes nitrogen down.
How to tell it apart

Guyabano drops leaves during long droughts (CTAHR), so check soil moisture before blaming nitrogen. Sulfur shortage also gives pale, small leaves, but it shows on the young leaves while the lower leaves look normal. To be sure, A leaf test shows low nitrogen. For guyabano, Brazilian work found the best leaves to sample are from the middle of branches in the middle third of the canopy.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Give nitrogen in small doses a few times a year, spread under the canopy and watered in. CTAHR gives a 10 10 10 fertilizer four times a year: about 0.23 kg per tree in total in the first year, 0.45 kg in the second. 1.4 kg a year after that. In the Philippines, Complete 14 14 14 is the usual complete fertilizer. Add Urea 46 0 0 or Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 when leaves are pale. Mix in manure or compost.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, feed in several small doses through the year rather than one big dose, keep a thick mulch over the shallow roots, and add manure every year.
Potassium deficiency in soursop

At first the foliage turns a deep green and the young leaves come out a little smaller. Then older leaves yellow along the margin, starting at the tip. The yellow moves inward between the veins, from yellow green to brown as the tissue dies. Other studies saw the edges turn orange yellow before browning. In severe cases the lower leaves fall and growth stops. These signs come from guyabano trials in Brazil and Venezuela. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees during fruit growth, and young trees on sandy soil.
Why potassium deficiency happens in guyabano

Sandy, leached soils and heavy rain, and years of fruiting with no potash returned. A Brazilian review notes that guyabano seedlings take up potash and nitrogen in the largest amounts of all nutrients.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium shortage also starts on older leaves, but it yellows along the midrib while the leaf margins stay green. Salt or fertilizer burn scorches margins quickly after a heavy dose. To be sure, A soil test for potash and a leaf test of leaves from the middle of branches in the middle third of the canopy.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or Sulfate of potash 0 0 50 under the canopy in split doses, following the soil test. A fertilizer with 3 percent nitrogen and 10 percent each of phosphate and potash has been used for guyabano in Cuba and Queensland (Morton). In the Philippines a Complete 14 14 14 plus Muriate of potash does the same job.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give potash in every feeding of bearing trees, and return fallen leaves and prunings as mulch.
Phosphorus deficiency in soursop

In a Brazilian trial the upper leaves showed it first: they came out narrower and smaller, with curved edges and tips pointing down. The lower leaves turned light green and were held close against the stem. Growth slowed sharply. Earlier trials saw the signs start on the lower leaves and move up. Leaving out phosphorus was the third most damaging omission for guyabano, after nitrogen and calcium. You see it most at this stage: seedlings and young trees, and trees on poor acid soils.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in guyabano
Acid and eroded soils low in organic matter, and no phosphate at planting. In a survey of guyabano orchards in Nayarit, Mexico, phosphorus was low in every orchard.
How to tell it apart

Nitrogen shortage gives an even pale yellow without the narrow, curled leaves. Mealybugs and scale insects, listed as guyabano pests by CTAHR, also weaken new growth. To be sure, A soil test for available phosphorus and pH. A leaf test of leaves from the middle of branches in the middle third of the canopy.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Work Superphosphate 0 20 0, 16 20 0 or Ammonium phosphate 18 46 0 into the soil under the canopy, following the soil test, together with manure or compost. CTAHR's 10 10 10 program and the 3 10 10 mix used in Cuba and Queensland both carry a good share of phosphate. Complete 14 14 14 can be used in the Philippines.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put phosphate and manure in the planting hole and give phosphate in the yearly feeding.
Calcium deficiency in soursop

The youngest leaves show it first: the leaf tip and the upper edge die and turn a burnt dark brown. While the rest of the leaf stays normal green. The burnt part rolls over on itself with the edges turned up. Later leaves drop early and the shoot tip stops growing. Earlier trials also saw yellowing around the edges and between the main veins before the tissue died. Leaving out calcium was the second most damaging omission after nitrogen. You see it most at this stage: young trees and new flushes, most often on acid soils.
Why calcium deficiency happens in guyabano
Strongly acid, leached soils low in calcium, which are common under heavy rainfall. Dry spells that slow calcium flow to the growing tips.
How to tell it apart

Potassium shortage burns the edges of older leaves first, not the newest leaves. Boron shortage also damages growing tips, but young leaves come out small and misshapen and fruit set fails. To be sure, A soil test for pH, calcium and magnesium. A leaf test of leaves from the middle of branches in the middle third of the canopy.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

On acid soils apply Agricultural lime or Dolomite under the canopy to raise the pH toward 5 to 6.5, the range CTAHR gives for guyabano. Take the amount from the soil test. Where the pH is already fine, Gypsum supplies calcium without changing the pH. TNAU gives Gypsum at 50 kg per hectare for custard apple, a close cousin. A Calcium nitrate spray on young flushes helps while the soil dose works. Follow the label.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, test the soil every few years and lime before the pH drops too low.
Boron deficiency in soursop

No guyabano particular description of boron shortage was found, so this follows general fruit tree signs. Young tissues suffer first: shoot tips stop growing and may die, and new leaves come out small and misshapen. Pollination and seed development fail, so fruit set is poor and fruits can grow lopsided or crack. A survey of guyabano orchards in Nayarit, Mexico found leaf boron low in every orchard. You see it most at this stage: flowering, fruit set and early fruit growth.
Why boron deficiency happens in guyabano
Sandy, leached and acid soils low in organic matter, and long dry spells. A Brazilian review notes boron and zinc matter most for annonas on acid tropical soils below pH 6.5.
How to tell it apart

Poor pollination is the main cause of low yield in guyabano (PROSEA), and it also gives lopsided fruits. So do not blame boron for every misshapen fruit. To be sure, A leaf test for boron of leaves from the middle of branches in the middle third of the canopy, and a soil test. Spray a few branches with boron before flowering and compare fruit set.
What to apply for boron deficiency
Apply Borax to the soil under the canopy or spray Solubor on the leaves before flowering, following the soil test and the label. Do not overdose, because too much boron burns leaf tips and edges.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add compost every year, and on sandy or acid soils include boron in the micronutrient sprays before flowering.
Magnesium deficiency in soursop

Older leaves in the middle of the plant show it first, with light yellowing along the midrib. The midrib and the side margins of the leaf stay green. As it gets worse the yellow band turns orange, the leaves drop early, and the plant grows less. Earlier trials described the same yellowing between the veins, starting beside the midrib and moving out to the edges. These signs come from guyabano trials in Brazil and Venezuela. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees and trees fed heavy potash, during fruit growth.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in guyabano
Acid, sandy and leached soils, and heavy potash fertilizer, which competes with magnesium.
How to tell it apart

Potassium shortage also starts on older leaves, but the yellow and brown start at the tip and margin and move inward. Nitrogen shortage yellows the whole leaf evenly, veins included. To be sure, A soil test for magnesium, potash and calcium together. A leaf test of leaves from the middle of branches in the middle third of the canopy.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

On acid soils apply Dolomite, which supplies both lime and magnesium. Take the amount from the soil test. Where the pH is already fine, spread Magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt) or Kieserite under the canopy and follow the label.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, balance potash with magnesium according to the soil test, and use Dolomite rather than plain lime on acid soils.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any soursop nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your guyabano needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Soursop nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my guyabano leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: lower leaves fade evenly to pale green, then the whole tree turns dull yellow and stays short. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at potassium deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in soursop?
items.a: Give nitrogen in small doses a few times a year, spread under the canopy and watered in. CTAHR gives a 10 10 10 fertilizer four times a year: about 0.23 kg per tree in total in the first year, 0.45 kg in the second.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in soursop?
items.a: Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or Sulfate of potash 0 0 50 under the canopy in split doses, following the soil test. A fertilizer with 3 percent nitrogen and 10 percent each of phosphate and potash has been used for guyabano in Cuba and Queensland (Morton).

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in soursop?
items.a: Work Superphosphate 0 20 0, 16 20 0 or Ammonium phosphate 18 46 0 into the soil under the canopy, following the soil test, together with manure or compost. CTAHR's 10 10 10 program and the 3 10 10 mix used in Cuba and Queensland both carry a good share of phosphate.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my guyabano lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the soursop nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
